newsitem.title: USA: FOCUS - Dow Jones cuts bonuses, union seeks review.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Dow Jones cuts bonuses, union seeks review.

text.p: Dow Jones & Co's lackluster stock performance in recent years hit the company's top executives in their wallets on Monday.
It also prompted the union that represents 2,500 Dow Jones employees to seek an independent performance review of the company's chairman and chief executive.
Dow Jones, publisher of the Wall Street Journal and Barron's and distributor of other financial news information services, said it reduced the bonuses it will pay its top managers for 1996.

The board of directors' compensation committee said in a proxy statement that Dow Jones' stock performance from 1993 to 1996 "was less than fully satisfactory, particularly as measured by three financial criteria given significant weight by the committee: stock price performance, total stockholder return and return on equity."

The news came on the same day that Standard & Poors lowered its corporate credit ratings and senior unsecured debt rating on Dow Jones to AA-minus from AA, and said its outlook for Dow Jones is now negative.

Analysts who follow the company said they were not surprised by the downgrading, which follows a recent announcement that Dow Jones would spend about $650 million to revamp its Telerate financial information services unit. The unit has since been renamed Dow Jones Markets.
Analysts also cited recent reports that some members of the families that hold a controlling interest in Dow Jones have expressed dissatisfaction with its stock performance.
"It does concern what we know: that they're going to have some earnings constraints," Smith Barney analyst John Reidy said of the downgrading.
Reidy added the new rating level is still competitive with other media companies.
The news did not affect Dow Jones' stock price, which held steady in afternoon trading and closed at 42-7/8, unchanged from Friday's close.

Chairman and Chief Executive Peter Kann had his annual bonus cut to $380,000 for 1996 compared to $445,000 in the prior year. President and Chief Operating Officer Kenneth Burenga's bonus was cut to $270,000 from $310,000; Senior Vice President Carl Valenti's was reduced to $155,000 from $220,000; and Senior Vice President Peter Skinner's dropped to $165,000 from $205,000.
Only Senior Vice President James Ottaway Jr's remained unchanged at $160,000.
The proposal for independent reviews of the chairman and chief executive was submitted by the Independent Association of Publishers' Employees, which represents employees at Dow Jones.
The union's proposal is to be voted on at the company's April 16 annual meeting. The union holds 55 shares of Dow Jones' common stock and 10 shares of its Class B common stock.
In recent months, Dow Jones has been under pressure from some members of the family that controls it.
Those family members have expressed dissatisfaction with the company's stock performance during recent years as much of the rest of the market has seen unprecedented gains.
Union President Ron Chen, a copy editor at the Wall Street Journal, said it has also been a lingering concern for the union.

"For some time, the union and the people who work here at Dow Jones have recognized there's something wrong with this company," Chen said. "We have been trying to somehow get the world to take a look at this company and find out what's going on."
The board of directors has opposed the union's proposal, saying it believes the steps are "unnecessary in light of the board's current policies and practices regarding executive compensation."
The board said its compensation committee evaluates the performance of top management each year.

"The board believes that it would not be in the company's best interest to base executive compensation solely on rigid or non-discretionary formulae since it is difficult to predict all future developments that could be relevant to evaluating management performance," it said in the proxy statement.
Dow Jones competes against Reuters Holdings Plc and Bloomberg LP in providing financial news and information in major markets.
